kjv: for the damsel's father had said unto the man
mine: Then the young woman's father said to the man
note: Wayyomer is a narrative sequential ('then he said'); the KJV's pluperfect makes the invitation precede the meal.

mine: and linger until the day declines
note: Hitmahmehu is an imperative, part of the father's speech ('linger until the day turns'), not a narrative statement that they stayed.

Beliyyaal is a common noun meaning 'worthlessness, wickedness'; the KJV's capitalised 'Belial' reads like a proper name of a demon, a sense it gains only in later Jewish and Christian usage (2 Cor 6:15).

mine: do not do this outrageous thing
note: Nevalah denotes a vile, shameful outrage (esp. sexual crime); modern 'folly' suggests mere foolishness.

kjv: divided her, together with her bones, into twelve pieces
mine: cut her up limb by limb into twelve pieces
note: Lafatseha means 'according to her bones', i.e. joint by joint, not 'along with her bones'.
